display.title: Episode 334: The Rambam's Grave (Yud-Gimmel Tammuz)
display.summary_short: The day after Yud-Beis Tammuz: the Frierdiker Rebbe's mesiras nefesh for children, a Geulah march, a first-grade class in Studio 604, and how a camel led the way to the Rambam's resting place.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 13 Tammuz 5748, the day after Yud-Beis Tammuz. Uncle Yossi recalls the Frierdiker Rebbe's release from prison and his readiness to give his life so that Jewish children could learn Torah. The Hakochainik march is a song of Geulah, 'Ki v'simchah seitzei'u', with Daniel's prophecy that heavenly clouds will carry the Jewish people to Eretz Yisroel. Story time begins: the Rambam passed away in Egypt asking to be buried in Eretz Yisroel without saying where, and the people of Yerushalayim, Chevron and Meron each claim the honor. In the desert, robbers attack the funeral caravan. A first-grade class from a Brooklyn yeshiva then says the Shema, reads the opening verses of Bereishis, and answers why the generation of the Tower of Bavel was punished less than the generation of the Flood: they had achdus. The story concludes: robbers who approach the coffin fall lifeless, the rest flee, and the camel, as if led by an unseen hand, walks to Teveria and kneels at the spot where the Rambam is buried. The show ends with a note that Shiva Asar B'Tammuz begins the Three Weeks and that this year both fasts are postponed to Sunday.
display.lesson: Hashem, the Guardian of Israel, guides and protects His tzaddikim; and Hashem loves achdus, unity among Jews.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: 'yesterday was Yud-Beis Tammuz'; Shiva Asar B'Tammuz 'this coming Shabbos'.

advisories.note: Armed robbers attack a funeral caravan in the desert; the people flee.
The story begins with the Rambam's passing; two robbers who approach his coffin fall dead.
Briefly explains that the Three Weeks recall the fall of Yerushalayim and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash.
